supporting_observations.claim: On FILE-ORC-01, svc-safe logged on shortly before C:\Program Files\Keystone\agent.exe started under that account with the command line targeting ingest.keystone-backup.net.

At 13:47:04, proxy telemetry recorded a 640,000,000-byte client-to-server transfer to ingest.keystone-backup.net, and Zeek recorded approximately 640 MB of originating traffic through the proxy. Windows filtering and Sysmon records associate the proxy connections with the Keystone agent process.

The transfer is consistent with the approved Keystone offsite backup activity: the inventory identifies this agent and endpoint as approved and says it uploads several hundred MB. This supports a benign disposition for the alerted transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records identify the destination and transfer volume, but do not establish the contents of the transferred data.
The available records do not establish the Keystone agent's file hash, signature, or integrity.
claims_not_established: The specific files or data included in the backup transfer.
Whether the agent binary was verified against a known-good hash or signature.
unrelated_findings: At 13:21, a Java process running as SYSTEM connected through the proxy to downloads.cloud.com. This service is not listed among the approved services; assess it separately. Records show the connection and process, but do not establish what was downloaded or whether it was malicious. (T280-00045, T280-00046, T280-00047, T280-00048)
